note: Live controls for internal/tui, the two-pane navigator. Golden frames are regression cover, not controls: a frame test fails on any byte diff and therefore proves nothing about a specific clause, which is this repository's dominant defect class wearing a costume. These sit on the load-bearing branches qy3de.11, qy3de.6 and qy3de.7 name — the cursor's id-tracking, the filter predicate, the truncation rule, the row set's status filter, the picker's row/line coordinate conversion, the direction of every relation heading, the modal's row-applicability logic, the editor's two refusals, the reopen prompt and the warning sink — split by branch where one clause is too coarse to mutate in one place. Seeded by qy3de.11; the follow half added by qy3de.12; the write set by qy3de.13; the poll, the stale marker and the redraw/retarget split by qy3de.14; esc's layer ordering by m3z5y. tc2x5 re-cut the redraw/retarget pair onto the two facts the pane can read — which issue is on screen, and the width it was rendered into — instead of the intent the caller passed, and split them three ways so each clause has a mutant the other two tests stay green for. g7b23 added `r`, the ready-only narrowing, and moved refresh to `R`: its controls sit on the predicate itself, on both directions of the toggle, and on each of the two paths that re-derive the visible row set — applyFilter and refresh — because a golden frame would pass whichever rows those returned. bvjgn added `y`: one control on the expression that chooses the id, because a test asserting only that some clipboard command came back passes with the cursor row's id in place of the pane's, one on the refusal an empty row set gets, and one on the LINE it reports through, because m.message would relayout both panes for a keystroke that wrote nothing and a test reading the footer alone would not notice.

controls.clause: The cursor tracks an issue ID and not a row index, so a reload that reorders rows cannot move the selection under the reader (qy3de.4, named there as a control rather than a preference)
When the tracked id leaves the row set — filtered out, closed with `C` off, deleted — the cursor holds the position index that row last occupied, clamped, rather than jumping to the top (qy3de.4)
`/` matches case-insensitively, so a lowercase needle finds a capitalised title (qy3de.4)
`/` is a substring over the id AND the title, because ids are structured and looking one up is half of what the filter is for (qy3de.4)

The ` [N]` marker is appended AFTER the title is cut, so the cut pays for it and a blocked row is never wider than its pane (euv2e.4 recorded this trap; qy3de.5 measured a 13-column marker leaving negative room on all 13 blocked rows)
The id column auto-sizes to the widest id present but never past twelve columns, because pad-to-widest spends twenty dead columns on 44 rows to fit two (qy3de.4)

An id past the cap is truncated through render's own ellipsis rule rather than overflowing its column — the pane deliberately breaks render's never-truncate-an-identifier rule, and the mark is what makes that honest (qy3de.3, qy3de.4)
The project column, shown only under `a`, is capped at twelve the same way: eight of the ten projects holding open issues have slugs of nine columns or fewer and cover 172 of 174 rows (qy3de.4)
The row set is `list`'s contract — open AND in_progress — not `ready`'s, because Ready and Blocked cannot see an in_progress issue and so would structurally hide the one you are working on (qy3de.4)
`C` includes closed issues in the row set, which is a 6.3x row jump in `drops` and is why it is disclosed in the footer as a word rather than a glyph (qy3de.4)
`r` keeps the rows with no OPEN blocker and nothing else — a local predicate over blockedBy the pane already holds, not core.Ready, which is a different question asked of the store (g7b23)
`r` hides the blocked rows (g7b23)
`r` is a TOGGLE: pressing it again brings the blocked rows back (g7b23)
`r` stacks with `/` and survives `a` and `C`, because applyFilter re-derives the visible set through the one function that applies both (g7b23)

`R` and every write go through refresh, which re-derives the visible set through the same function, so a blocked issue written by somebody else does not appear on a pane told to hide exactly that (g7b23)
controls.new:
m.all = rows
	m.rows = matching(m.all, m.filter)
	m.cursor.restore(m.rows)

controls.clause: `r` leaving no visible rows says `No ready issues · r to show blocked`, so a fully blocked project is not misreported as empty (d3kty)
An overflowing footer truncates its plain text before applying the dim style, so the emitted SGR reset survives and the footer cannot leak colour past the frame (edgud)
`y` copies the RIGHT PANE'S issue id, not the row under the cursor. The two differ under a follow trail, where the right pane is the issue you are reading and the object `x` already names (bvjgn)
`y` on an empty row set sends nothing and reports nothing, rather than naming an empty id as sent — the refusal `x` already makes there (bvjgn)

`y` acknowledges through m.notice, which replaces the footer's left side and dies on the next keypress, and NOT m.message, which costs a pane row via messageLines and would relayout both panes for a keystroke that changed nothing about the store — qy3de.14 §Q5's argument for the stale marker run the other way (bvjgn)
The detail pane renders through render.Console into a buffer at the MEASURED pane width, so a resize re-wraps the page rather than clipping one wrapped for the old width (qy3de.3)
controls.old: console := render.Console{Out: &buf, Width: width, TTY: false}
controls.new: console := render.Console{Out: &buf, Width: render.DefaultWidth, TTY: false}

controls.clause: lipgloss Style.Width is the TOTAL rendered width, borders included, so a pane of N content columns asks for N+2 — getting it backwards leaves the top edge and the body two columns apart (qy3de.2, qy3de.5)

Heights are managed by pad and never by a Style, because lipgloss Height() is the OUTER height and leaving it to a Style left the two panes at different heights (euv2e.4's trap, paid for in one place by qy3de.5)
The footer names the visible column window and the widest line whenever the page overflows the pane and is not wrapped, so a clipped table row does not read as a whole row (qy3de.5)
picker.move clamps the cursor to [0, len(rows)-1] at both ends, which is also what makes `g` and `G` a delta longer than the list rather than two more branches (qy3de.6 §10 control 1)

view emits a group header exactly where the group CHANGES — not once per row (qy3de.6 §10 control 2). Headers are never stored as rows, which is what removes the skip-the-header branch rather than testing it

The same clause's other wrong implementation: a header emitted only above the FIRST row leaves every later group unlabelled, which is what a picker over seven relation kinds cannot survive (qy3de.6 §5, §10 control 2)
scroll windows on the cursor's RENDERED LINE, not its row index — the one place the two coordinates disagree, because every header above a row shifts it down (qy3de.6 §10 control 3)

view re-derives the same window from the cursor's rendered line, so a picker drawn without a scroll — after a resize, or in a test — still shows the row under the cursor (qy3de.6 §10 control 3, the second place the conversion happens)

A `blocks` OUT edge is what blocks this issue and an IN edge is what this issue blocks: the direction is named from the reader's end, the opposite of the edge's own (qy3de.6 §10 control 4). A swapped pair survives a round trip and reads plausibly, which is why each kind is its own control

`A discovered-from B` means A was derived from B, so the OUT edge is where this issue came from — `Discovered from` — and the IN edge is what came out of it — `Discovered` (qy3de.6 §5, §10 control 4). The page has an independent control for its mapping; this control keeps the picker's separate branch from swapping the pair
`related` is undirected, so it is ONE group holding core's merge of both directions rather than a pair of headings named from an end that does not exist (qy3de.6 §5; the merge moved to core by y7f6z)

The picker's id column auto-sizes to the widest id IN THAT PICKER and does NOT inherit the left pane's twelve-column cap: a picker's rows are by construction siblings, and seven of gitops-vn4's sixteen live children collapse to the same twelve columns (qy3de.6 §4, §10 control 5)
`f` on an issue with no relations opens nothing and says `nothing to follow`, rather than an empty modal that captures every key with nothing to choose (qy3de.6 §2, §10 control 6)
`backspace` at depth 0 is a no-op, not a pop off an empty stack (qy3de.6 §10 control 7)

Moving the left cursor clears the follow stack. This is the control under a key REMOVED from the design: euv2e.5's `esc clears the stack` was dropped because `j` — a key you were about to press — already does it (qy3de.6 §7, §10 control 8)
`x` on a tombstoned issue opens no modal at all and says so, because every core write refuses one with ErrConflict and a modal of six verbs that all fail is worse than none (qy3de.7 §8)
The modal offers `close` on live work and `reopen` on a closed issue, never both and never the wrong one (qy3de.7 §8)

`claim` and `release` are withheld from a closed issue even though ClaimIssue permits one: 38 of the live store's 39 assignees sit on closed issues, so the claim is the durable record of who resolved a ticket (qy3de.7 §8)
`release` appears only on a claimed issue and `claim` only on an unclaimed one, so neither verb is ever offered where core would refuse it (qy3de.7 §8)

`x` acts on whatever the RIGHT PANE is showing — the followed target when the stack is non-empty, the cursor's issue otherwise. euv2e.6 said "the right pane's issue" before there was a follow stack that could make the two differ (qy3de.7 §8)
An empty or whitespace-only editor file writes no close at all — a real divergence from the CLI, where `--reason` is optional and `drops close <id>` legally stores NULL (qy3de.7 §3)
An empty or whitespace-only editor file writes no comment AND says nothing: letting core refuse it as ErrInvalid would put an error on the message line for something that did not happen (qy3de.7 §3)
A non-zero editor exit discards the file however full it is, which is what makes `:cq` a deliberate cancel rather than a silent loss (qy3de.7 §3)

`reopen`'s prompt reports the ACTUAL length of the close_reason SetIssueStatus is about to null out. It is not an "are you sure": it states the size of what is lost, which is the one thing the reader cannot otherwise see (qy3de.7 §7)
Every key but `y` answers the reopen prompt with no, so a keypress that was not an answer cannot destroy a close reason (qy3de.7 §7)
A credential pattern in a comment body produces a VISIBLE line rather than a silent stderr write, which under an alt screen is the same as no warning at all (qy3de.7 §5)

A write refused by core — realistically a claim landing between the render and the `enter` — leaves the store as it was and says so on the message line, which is the only place it can be seen under a full-screen program (qy3de.7 §10)

The re-read after a write RESTORES the cursor onto its tracked id rather than holding an index, so a priority change — which re-orders the list, since `ORDER BY issues.priority` is the store's first key — carries the cursor to the row's new position instead of selecting someone else (qy3de.7 §9)
The message line is taken out of the PANES, so qy3de.4's disclosure line and qy3de.5's scroll indicator are undisturbed while it is up, and the row comes back when it clears (qy3de.7 §10)

A tick NOTICES and does not refresh: the poll raises the stale marker and leaves the row set exactly where the reader had it, because a surface that reorders itself mid-thought is what this map exists to avoid, and on this store the common writer is an agent (qy3de.14 §Q1)

The one path that handles a tickMsg returns another tick. There is no second timer to notice the first one died, so a branch that returns nil stops the poll for the rest of the session with nothing on screen to say so (qy3de.14 §Q4)
Init arms the first tick, which is the one thing Run cannot do: a tea.Cmd is only run by a Program, so arming it anywhere else drops it on the floor (qy3de.14 §Q4)
The marker is DERIVED from the two sequence numbers rather than being a flag a write could forget to clear: stale is exactly observed != seq (qy3de.14 §Q5)
controls.old: func (m *Model) stale() bool { return m.observed != m.seq }

controls.clause: The marker outlives the next keypress, unlike both transient slots: it is a state of the store, not a line about something that just happened, so pressing `j` while the store is still ahead must not clear it (qy3de.14 §Q5)

The marker is a FOOTER part and never the message line: messageLines feeds geo, which every caller measures from, so a marker on the message row would shrink both panes by a row while a picker was open and re-scroll it under the cursor (qy3de.14 §Q5)

A failed refresh keeps the old rows and therefore keeps their sequence state: the token read before source.rows is committed only after that read succeeds, so clearing the transient error cannot leave stale rows reporting fresh (hc6jb)
The refresh that reads past the change is what clears the marker, and nothing else does: readRows marks the pane fresh as of the token it took before reading those rows (qy3de.14 §Q5)

`R` re-reads whether or not the pane believes itself stale. An override that silently declines is the key you press twice, and a conditional one puts a branch on state the reader cannot see — the argument qy3de.6 used to drop the one-relation shortcut (qy3de.14 §Q6)

`r` keeps the follow stack, because re-reading the store is not a navigation. reload clears it — that is what moving the cursor does — so spending reload here would drop a reader out of a followed page every time they checked for changes (qy3de.14 §Q6)
controls.old:
// re-reading the store is not a navigation.
		m.fail(m.refresh())
controls.new:
// re-reading the store is not a navigation.
		m.fail(m.reload())

controls.clause: Redrawing the SAME page holds the reader's scroll offsets: a refresh that reset them would throw a reader scrolled deep into a long page back to line 0 every time an agent wrote anything, which on this store is the common case (qy3de.14 §Q2)

A width change reflows the page, so the offset the reader left behind names a line that is no longer the one they were reading: `enter`-zoom, the `esc` out of it and a terminal resize all start the page at the top, where a redraw at the SAME width holds. The width is the second of the two facts showDetail decides on, and the one that keeps deleting the `keep` flag from moving any motion that was not broken (tc2x5)

The other half of the same branch: opening a DIFFERENT page starts it at the top, whether the reader opened it with `j` or a refresh's cursor restore walked onto it (tc2x5). It is decided on IDENTITY and not on the caller's intent, which is what the old `keep` flag got wrong: refresh redrew with keep=true at whatever id the restore landed on, so a page the reader had never scrolled opened at the offset of the page they were reading (qy3de.14 §Q2)

A page counts as unchanged only when its RENDERED TEXT is identical. A comment is its own record with its own revision, so Issue.Revision is unmoved by the write most likely to change the page you are reading, and a revision test would decline to re-render exactly that (qy3de.14 §Q2)

§Q7's guard, written as a test rather than as code: a refresh is unreachable from inside a modal because modalKey's switch has no `R`, and this is what would catch a future key that gave it one. The suppression this ticket considered building would have been a branch whose control could never go red (qy3de.14 §Q7)
controls.new:
case "ctrl+c":
		return tea.Quit
	case "R":
		m.fail(m.refresh())
	case "esc":
		m.closeModal()

controls.clause: §Q7's guard applied to g7b23's second key: `r` is unreachable from inside a modal because modalKey's switch has no `r` either, so a picker cannot re-cut the row set under the reader looking at it
controls.new:
case "ctrl+c":
		return tea.Quit
	case "r":
		m.readyOnly = !m.readyOnly
		m.fail(m.applyFilter())
	case "esc":
		m.closeModal()

controls.clause: `esc` closes the help screen (m3z5y: the first of the layers escape() orders)
`esc` pops ONE layer, and the help screen is taken before the follow stack, so an esc under the help leaves the trail standing (m3z5y)
`esc` clears the WHOLE follow stack in one press, where `backspace` pops one level (m3z5y, reversing qy3de.6 §7)
Clearing the stack with `esc` retargets the right pane at the id the LIST CURSOR holds, without moving the cursor — the founding claim `j` could not satisfy because selectRow moves it (m3z5y)
`esc` takes the follow stack before the filter, so returning to the cursor's issue does not also discard what narrowed the list (m3z5y)
Zoom is the LAST layer `esc` pops, which is what makes a sixth meaning safe: it fires only on a press that had nothing else to take (m3z5y)
`esc` unzooms once nothing else is live (m3z5y, the one open sub-question the ticket left: answered yes)
The help screen captures every key while it is up, so nothing acts invisibly behind it — in particular `x` cannot open a modal that would then swallow the `esc` meant to close the help (m3z5y)
`ctrl+c` quits the full-screen TUI from the top-level keymap instead of being swallowed (9cta5)
controls.old:
case "q", "ctrl+c":
		// A full-screen program that swallows ctrl+c
controls.new:
case "q":
		// A full-screen program that swallows ctrl+c

controls.clause: `ctrl+c` quits the full-screen TUI while a modal is open instead of being captured by the modal (9cta5)
`ctrl+c` quits the full-screen TUI while the `/` filter prompt is open instead of being swallowed as a non-printable key (9cta5)
